objective: Replace mutable live-source historical reproduction dependencies with immutable published benchmark snapshots while preserving live sources as drift-monitoring/reference lanes.

baseline.description: Live ALeRCE drift blocked exact historical reproduction; 730,184 membership was being reconstructed from current light-curve artifacts.

correctness.after: immutable published ALeRCE and CPVS reference contracts pinned

reliability.before: live mutable service required for historical validation
reliability.after: archive MD5/SHA-256 validation with fail-closed acquisition

reproducibility.before: CPVS current-source derivation and live ALeRCE could drift
reproducibility.after: published 730,184 membership and ALeRCE 2020-06-09 snapshot are immutable reference inputs

measurement.trade_off: Current-source derivation remains diagnostic; it is not silently promoted to the historical published benchmark.

evidence: Zenodo 4279623 provides the historical ALeRCE labeled set, features, and classifier outputs through 2020-06-09.
Zenodo 5764899 provides the published 730,184-object CPVS quality-selected population.
Archive acquisition utility validates published MD5 and records SHA-256/member evidence.
Live ALeRCE remains reference/drift monitoring and is not treated as ground truth.

root_causes: Historical ALeRCE blocker was caused by mutable live data replacing an immutable 2020 snapshot.
CPVS exact-count reconstruction from present-day source artifacts is a reproduction diagnostic, not a valid replacement for the published membership release.

findings: Published benchmark membership and deterministic source reconstruction must be separate evidence lanes.
Historical classifier parity can be validated against an archived feature/output release without requiring current API equality.
The public ZTF ecosystem consistently uses versioned/frozen catalogs and explicit data provenance.

open_blockers: The new immutable artifacts still need to be acquired in CI before final release-gate closure.
CPVS source-derivation mismatch remains diagnostic evidence, not an acceptance blocker.
Live ALeRCE drift remains monitored independently.
